refuter_contract.atom_support: the support report's identified mass equals the posterior weight of the atoms the identifier accepts (1 when all are, 0.65 when a 0.35 atom is a directed cycle)

oracle.method: Closed forms: the front-door curve E[Y | do(t)] = sum_m P(m | t) g(m), g(m) = sum_t' P(t') P(Y=1 | m, t') of the exact 1000-row table gives [0.314, 0.596] and the mean outcome 0.386, the level of the flat curve a permuted treatment must give; the Cpdag law y = t + z + e has the curve a and the PAG law y = 1 + 2 t + 0.8 z + e the curve 1 + 2 a on the grid [0, 1] (population values, E z = 0; the doubly robust sampled curve is checked within 0.25 on 1500 rows). The refuter contract lists the refuters each graph-posterior curve study runs at each depth and inference mode (validation-suite design, not derivable); some refuters are refused for a curve and recorded as such.
oracle.formula: front door: sum_m P(m | t) sum_t' P(t') P(y | m, t'); cpdag: a; pag: 1 + 2 a
asserted_outputs: refuter_contract (refuters that run and pass; the placebo curve is flat at the mean outcome)
oracle.independence_basis: The generator evaluates the front-door formula on the stated table probabilities in exact rationals; it imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The shared object is the stated table and laws.
oracle.historical_exposure: Written for this fixture from the stated law and the declared inputs; no product implementation source was consulted to obtain the values.

reference_review.limitations: The Cpdag and PAG curves are population values for a simulated sample, checked within a wide band because the Frequentist curve is a doubly robust estimate; the front-door curve is exact for the Frequentist plug-in and within a stated band for the Dirichlet posterior mean. The refuter contract is a validation-suite design choice asserted by the executing tests. No coverage or calibration claim.
